ideas.title: The dowsing stone on a cord
ideas.critique: Spikes leaping to the magnet stone again repeat the payoff of The magnet stone. What is new is that Lumi holds the stone and steers a real pendulum through the field, which ends the run of objects moving alone under a fixed camera. The swing that leans toward hidden iron is a readable, learnable mechanic, if the cord and the beak hold really read on screen.

ideas.title: Two stones under one patch: where is it?
ideas.critique: Iron filings showing field lines is a textbook picture, and a top-down view of grains turning is close to the dim compass film's single needle quietly obeying the field. The guessing game with random poses and friends who really dig is a real goal that changes every round, which no earlier field film had.

ideas.title: Strike a light: sparks from a stone
ideas.critique: Glowing hot things lighting the dusk has been done once (the hot glass), but a particle system of burning iron shavings, each with its own oxidation heat and blackbody glow, and fire caught on tinder by skill is something the island never had. It fits the big goal's title more than its road, which is electricity, not fire.

ideas.title: The tongue test
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: A first circuit solved from what touches what is a real road step, and Lumi's crest bristling is a funny, readable current meter. The risk is that the visible result is a face reaction keyed to a number, so it plays as an animation picked from a table unless the cell building itself is hands-on.

ideas.title: What is it made of? The beach test
ideas.critique: A materials table is backbone work that the big goal needs. As a film it is a sorting minigame with yes/no answers, and the bronze-bell surprise is mild. Its value is in what it unlocks, not in what someone watching sees.

ideas.title: The bellows and the green rock
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is the glowing hot-craft recipe again (glass, then kiln), and a lumped kiln model with a reduction threshold is close to a rig made for one case. A rhythm the player can learn and the first real copper are the strong part, and it clears a road step.

ideas.title: The draw plate
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Copper worked at a bench and shown close up is the wire-bending post's form again. Work hardening and annealing are a real mechanism to feel, but the payoff a viewer sees, a wire getting longer and then snapping, is small.

ideas.title: The scrap crane
ideas.critique: Iron flying to a source is the magnet stone payoff again, but a coil the player winds and switches, with lift set by turns and cells, plus dropping spikes on a friend, is a toy people come back to. It depends on a cell circuit and a winding mechanic that do not exist yet, so a first session may only show a fraction of it.

ideas.title: Where lightning goes
ideas.critique: Dielectric breakdown grown on a real Laplace solve is a spectacle no game agent is expected to make, and the traced bolt light is a RayMakie showcase. The player's part is putting up a rod and waiting for a storm, and it sits beside the road, not on it.

ideas.title: A speaker made of paper and a coil
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Hearing a homemade speaker is a lovely payoff, and the force on a current in the stone's field is genuine big-goal physics. But a cone shivering on film is hard to see, and a mass-spring-damper cone with one turns knob is close to a one-case rig.
